messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — onboarding siren-17b (int4) is hitting intermittent OOMs on 48GB nodes during bursts. Repro on canary yesterday afternoon.
omar: seeing it too. pattern looks like bursts where batch concurrency spikes to 6+ and max_new_tokens=1024. memory climbs then slab fragmentation prevents evict.
lisa: confirmed. low tail requests with long max_new_tokens allocate huge KV windows. p95 memory jumps before OOM.
anya: repro steps I used:
```bash
# run locally on canary node
curl -X POST https://canary-api/redeem -d '{"model":"siren-17b","prompt":"<...>","max_new_tokens":1024}'
# tail logs:
journalctl -u runtime -f | grep siren-17b
```
mike: stack trace snippet from node: "AllocationError: failed to allocate 2.3GiB contiguous slab; free fragments: 1.2GiB" — that smells like fragmentation rather than raw memory shortage.
anya: yes — allocator shows many small free segments after sustained micro-batching. Prefetching KV windows makes it worse.
omar: quick mitigation idea: lower default max_new_tokens for this model to 512, clamp per-request batch_tokens to 1024, and enforce max_batch_size=4. Also enable soft-evict and kv_trim on route.
lisa: agree. also try turning on small-slot compaction (slot_reserve: 0.05) to reduce fragmentation. we had good luck with that on klystron.
anya: proposed route patch (canary):
```yaml
model: siren-17b
quant: int4
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 512
  max_batch_size: 4
  batch_tokens: 1024
heuristics:
  kv_prefetch: true
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.75
  soft_evict: true
  slot_reserve: 0.05
```
omar: +1. also add an emergency fallback to siren-17b-8k (same model with smaller context) if memory pressure > 85% for 30s.
mike: can we add a short jittered-burst throttle to the front-end too? that will smooth spikes while we canary.
anya: will open PR with the route change + throttling hook and a post-deploy smoke test. tests to include: 1) 10 concurrent sessions with max_new_tokens=512, 2) ramp to 20 sessions with mixed token lengths.
lisa: monitoring checklist: OOM count, slab fragmentation ratio, p50/p95 latency, canary error-rate. If OOMs drop <1/hr and slab ratio improves, roll to prod.
anya: deploy-bot — can you schedule a 30m canary on rack-7 tonight at 02:00 UTC? tagging infra for visibility. :pray:
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: siren-17b route patch -> rack-7, window 2024-04-02T02:00:00Z for 30m. Notifying eng-ml and eng-infra.
mike: I'll be on-call for the window and watch allocator metrics. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
